text: To be bumped off a flight
Having cleared immigration, he went looking for the shuttle.
Arriving at midnight, you see almost nothing of a city.
Given the delay, the connection was never going to work.
With the border closed, onward travel was impossible.
Third night this month I have slept in a terminal. Having done it enough times, I have a system, and the system is mostly about not being angry.
That is the part I find hardest. Not the waiting — the pointlessness of the waiting.
The queue at that desk will not move faster because two hundred of us are furious. Faced with that, I go and find the one person who actually has information.
And how do you find them? Because at three in the morning everybody in uniform says the same thing.
You ask a question they can answer. Not when will the flight go, which nobody knows, but is there anybody here who can rebook me tonight. Specific questions find specific people.
Which is a good rule well beyond airports. Did you get onward travel in the end?
Eventually. Not knowing whether the border would reopen, I booked a hotel for two nights and a flight for the third. It cost more and I slept.
Having spent a career being woken at three in the morning, I would say that is the correct answer.
Can you rebook me tonight, on any airline?
Having landed at two in the morning, I would rather have any bed than the right flight.
Given the delay, my connection is gone. What are my options?
I have proof of onward travel on my phone.
The hotel is a stone's throw from the station — which exit do I want?

Ladies and gentlemen, this is an announcement for passengers travelling on the delayed service to Istanbul. Regrettably this flight will not now depart this evening. The border has closed to overflights and our crew have reached the end of their permitted hours. Hotel accommodation will be provided and vouchers are being distributed at the gate. Please note that rebooking cannot be carried out at this gate. Passengers with onward connections should proceed to the transfer desk in the arrivals hall, which is on the level below, and which will remain open. Passengers without onward connections should remain here. We are extremely sorry for the disruption to your journey this evening, and we will make a further announcement within the hour.

I have worked nights on a transfer desk for eleven years, so let me tell you what actually works, because it is not what people think. The single most useful thing you can do is ask a question I am able to answer. When will the flight go? I do not know, nobody in this building knows, and asking me twelve times will not change that. Can you rebook me tonight, on any airline, to anywhere within two hundred kilometres of my destination? That I can work with. Second thing. Shouting fails, and not for the reason people assume. It is not that we take offence. It is that the person you are shouting at usually has no authority to change anything, and the person who does have that authority is standing behind them deciding who to help first. And third, and I mean this quite literally: we remember the calm ones. At three in the morning, being remembered is worth a great deal.

She explains that she leaves the queue and looks for the one person with information. He asks how she finds that person at three in the morning. She answers that specific questions find specific people, and describes the question she asks.
